children: GeoComputing Group, a leading provider of high-performance petro-technical solutions for the energy sector, and Gold Hydrogen Limited (

), a world-leading natural hydrogen and helium explorer, have entered a Memorandum of Understanding that will evaluate the use of AViR, GeoComputing’s private data and AI platform to support Gold Hydrogen’s technical teams and decision-making.

The MoU will assess the potential to upgrade Gold Hydrogen’s SharePoint-based technical information repository and integrate large language model and agentic AI capabilities. The objective is to make geological and technical information – including legacy PDFs, well completion reports and well logs – easier to search, retrieve, trace and analyze.

“To advance natural hydrogen and helium exploration in Australia, we are partnering with GeoComputing to build a localized LLM and multi-agent AI platform that automatically processes and extracts critical insights from our complex geoscience data," said Billy Hadi Subrata, CTO of Gold Hydrogen. “This MoU affords us an evaluation period to discover how these capabilities may enhance any potential project or service that we might develop. We are eager to see exactly how AViR will unlock new insights to make our exploration efforts even stronger.”

AViR expands upon GeoComputing’s RiVA cloud platform by delivering the computing performance needed while helping technical teams put their knowledge to work – all within a private setting that allows them to retain control over their environment. RiVA provides the foundation for demanding petroleum workflows by bringing high-performance computing close to the data it depends on while AViR extends that environment via locally hosted language models designed for private, in-country operation.
Key advantages that AViR delivers to operators in the energy sector include enhancing knowledge retrieval, bringing AI closer to critical E&P workloads and gaining predictable AI economies at scale.

“Having advantages of AI-based knowledge retrieval as part of a private, local deployment model can significantly enhance the exploration of naturally occurring hydrogen and helium,” said John Creevan, CEO of GeoComputing. “By entering a memorandum of understanding with Gold Hydrogen, we hope to showcase the ability of AViR to deliver those advantages by giving their technical team the tools that will enhance their productivity while containing costs. We look forward to the positive results we anticipate generating when working with Gold Hydrogen and having it serve as a springboard for future success.”

Gold Hydrogen Limited engages in the discovery, exploration, and development of natural hydrogen and helium gas in Australia. The company’s flagship project owned 100% interest of the Ramsay project covering an area of approximately 75,000 square kilometers located on the Yorke Peninsula and Kangaroo Island in South Australia. The company was incorporated in 2021 and is based in Brisbane, Australia.

GeoComputing Group, founded in 2004, is an IT consultancy for oil, gas, energy, and other geoscience companies. Its services include bespoke solution design and architecture, project management, infrastructure services, application support, and data management. In addition, it offers RiVA, the most powerful platform in the E&P industry, combining core components from leading vendors into a single, highly efficient and highly performant computing environment customized for petro-technical workflows. GeoComputing’s follow-the-sun support provides subject-matter experts in infrastructure, data, geoscience applications and workflows 24/7/365. For product information visit https://www.geocomputing.com/products.html and follow the company at https://www.linkedin.com/company/geocomputing-group-llc.
